inconsistencies: Two overlapping typed-settings efforts: #31260 says it is the compile-time foundation for runtime validation in #16545 and #22978, while #16545 presents itself as the base of its own stack (#17580, #17783, #17493). Reviewers should settle which is the base before either lands; review #31260 and #16545 together.

Argsman stack order matters and must be reviewed in sequence: #16545 -> #17580 -> {#17783, #17493} -> #17581. #17581 (P4) is only correct because #17493 forbids the duplicate assignments it removes handling for, so it cannot merge first.
util::Result chain: #25665 -> #26022 -> #25722, with #29700 also built on #25665. #26022 must be reviewed before #25722; #25665 is the single unblocking item.
Logging stack: #34778 -> #29256 -> #30342 (#30342 additionally needs #33847). #34778 was scored a band below the P2 work it unblocks; it has been raised so the base is not below its dependents.

#34038 and #35387 solve the same problem (trace logging is unusable without a paired -debug flag, and cannot be toggled by RPC) by competing designs; a reviewer flagged the overlap. #34038 should be reviewed first because #35355 and #34730 are built on it.

#35322 and #35355 both replace the mutex-protected per-category log level map with atomic bitmasks; they are duplicate solutions to the same lock-overhead problem and should be reconciled rather than reviewed independently.

#36880, #36861, #16545 and #17783 all attack variants of the same argument-handling footgun (negated or mistyped options silently becoming "0" or being ignored). Deciding the overall approach once would avoid four partially overlapping patches; #36880 documents the concrete user-visible harms and should anchor that discussion.
#36442 -> #36443 (-> #36444) descriptor chain: #36443 cannot be evaluated before #36442 establishes the single multipath Descriptor representation.
#36768 is presented as an alternative to the single-connection approach in #34775; only one should be pursued, and the concurrency change it introduces to callbacks needs an explicit decision.
result.notes: The solo assessments produced no P1 at all, which under-uses the band in a category whose stated first priority is correctness and safety of shared primitives. Four PRs were promoted: a crash regression on disk-write failure (#36049), a remotely triggerable memory-exhaustion vector in deserialization (#36906), an out-of-bounds read in the JSON tokenizer (#35281), and a cluster of hazardous negated-option defaults including an assertion crash (#36880). Two P3s were promoted for consequence (#36716 remote busy-spin, #36861 unvalidated numeric options) and one for dependency order (#34778, base of P2 logging work). The list is otherwise dominated by three long stacks (argsman/settings, util::Result, logging macros); within each, position follows dependency order rather than individual score, which accounts for most of the large position shifts.
